facts: JanusDDG is a model developed by the Computational Biomedicine Unit at the University of Turin.
The team that developed JanusDDG includes researchers Guido Barducci and Ivan Rossi.
JanusDDG predicts sequence-based protein stability using a thermodynamics-compliant approach.
The model employs a two-fronts multi-head attention mechanism.
JanusDDG is a deep learning framework that predicts the change in Gibbs free energy (ΔΔG) from mutations.
The model uses protein language model (PLM) embeddings and a bidirectional cross-attention transformer.
JanusDDG outperforms traditional structure-based methods in predicting ΔΔG.
The code for JanusDDG can be found at https://github.com/compbiomed-unito/JanusDDG.

The study quantifies protein stability using the change in Gibbs free energy (∆∆𝐺). A positive ∆∆𝐺 indicates a stabilizing mutation. The research introduces JanusDDG, a deep learning model for predicting ∆∆𝐺. JanusDDG incorporates antisymmetry and transitivity to enhance prediction accuracy.
JanusDDG is a sequence-based model for predicting protein stability.
The model utilizes bidirectional cross-attention to integrate wild-type and mutant sequence information.
JanusDDG was evaluated on benchmark datasets S669, S461, and S96.
The model classifies mutations as stabilizing, neutral, or destabilizing.
JanusDDG is a new sequence-based deep learning model for predicting protein stability changes due to mutations.
JanusDDG uses a bidirectional cross-attention architecture combined with protein language model embeddings.
The model excels in predicting the effects of multiple mutations compared to existing models.
The authors suggest future validation of JanusDDG across diverse mutation spectra and structural classes.
The JanusDDG model predicts protein stability changes due to mutations.
The datasets used include blind test datasets S669, S461, S96, and PTmul-NR.
Performance metrics for evaluating the model include Pearson and Spearman correlation coefficients.
The JanusDDG architecture utilizes a Bidirectional Cross-Attention Transformer with ESM2 embeddings.
JanusDDG FineTuned achieved the highest Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.83 on the S461 test set.
The JanusDDG only Antisym. model enforces antisymmetry in predictions.
JanusDDG has a mean squared error of 2.10 on the Q3421 dataset.
JanusDDG FineTuned is an enhanced version of the JanusDDG Base model.
